Predicted seagrass carbon map at Cadiz Bay for 2024 and 2025

Lee, Chengfa Benjamin

2026-05-21

This page documents the results of the Zostera noltii seagrass carbon mapping work at Cadiz Bay. This includes work done in:

  • Coring Carbon Seagrass by Simon Oiry
  • Exploring the relationship between seagrass reflectance and biomass
  • Measuring the carbon content in Zostera noltii seagrass

All analyses were performed in R version 4.5.2 (R Core Team 2025). All work belong to the REWRITE project.

1 Study Location

This page focuses on Cadiz Bay, a demonstrator site for the REWRITE PROJECT. There is an extensive seagrass meadow along the bay.

The sites were sampled according to transect lines.

2 ICE CREAMS Model prediction

For the purpose of map display and data analysis, the result from the Sentinel-2 image on 14 June 2025 was chosen. This date falls within the fieldwork dates and is thus best for validation and groundtruthing. Post-classification, any pixels with a class probability of less than 85% were masked out.

3 Seasonal change

Figure 3.1: Annual mean NDVI value of pixels classified by the ICE CREAMS model as seagrass from 2016 to 2025. The black line denotes the actual mean NDVI values while the blue line and grey ribbons are the geom_smooth values. The dotted red line indicates the chosen date (2025-06-14) showcased in the previous section.

Zoffoli et al. (2020) established a relationship between NDVI and seagrass percent cover: \[Seagrass\,percent\,cover\,(SPC) = 172.06*NDVI - 22.18\]

Conventionally in remote sensing, the extent was calculated by multiplying the number of pixels labelled as the class of interest and the pixel area. This approach tends to overestimate the extent, as many of the classified/labelled pixels might be mixed. By exploiting that a Sentinel-2 pixel of its best spatial resolution is 100m^{2} and that seagrass percent cover ranges from 0-100%, Davies et al. (2024) was able to make a relationship between the estimated extent and the cover: \[Seagrass\,extent\,in\,a\,pixel = SPC\]

This provides a better estimate of the seagrass extent per pixel and reduce the overestimation. To reduce possible overestimation, pixels with less than 20% seagrass cover and pixels without the seagrass label are excluded from the calculation. \[Total\,seagrass\,extent = \sum SPC,\,where\,SPC>=20\,and\,pixels\,classified\,as\,seagrass\]

Figure 3.2: Annual total seagrass extent of pixels classified by the ICE CREAMS model as seagrass from 2016 to 2025, by assuming that every percent in the seagrass cover is equivalent to 1 m^2. The black line denotes the predicted extent while the blue line and grey ribbons are the geom_smooth values. The dotted red line indicates the chosen date (2025-06-14) showcased in the previous section.

Figure 3.3: Total seagrass extent of pixels classified by the ICE CREAMS model as seagrass from 2016 to 2025, by assuming that every percent in the seagrass cover is equivalent to 1 m^2. The black line denotes the predicted extent while the blue line and grey ribbons are the geom_smooth values. The dotted red line indicates the chosen date (2025-06-14) showcased in the previous section.

5 Carbon stock prediction

The soil carbon estimate was extracted from the soil carbon values in Cadiz Bay reported in Santos et al. (2023), which was based on the upper 1m sediment layer.

6 Seasonal change in seagrass biomass

Figure 6.1: Predicted biomass values of the aboveground, belowground and total components of the seagrass meadows in Cadiz Bay from 2016 to 2025. There were no biomass in the soil component.

Figure 6.2: Predicted carbon values of the aboveground and belowground components of the seagrass meadows in Cadiz Bay from 2016 to 2025. The total carbon estimate included the aboveground carbon estimate, belowground carbon estimate and the soil carbon estimate. The soil carbon estimate was extracted from the soil carbon values in Cadiz Bay reported in Santos et al. (2023), which was based on the upper 1m sediment layer.
